name: TASKI autonomous sweeper and scrubber robots at Houston Bush Intercontinental
summary: Houston Airports said on October 30 that four TASKI cleaning robots are now working at George Bush Intercontinental (IAH), making it the first U.S. airport to deploy the company's combination of autonomous sweepers and scrubbers. The machines went into operational use the week of August 10. A compact TASKI Phantas sweeps, vacuums, scrubs and dust-mops in the Terminal E security queue, an Ecobot 50 scrubs and dries the Terminal E mezzanine, and two Ecobot 40 sweepers work the Terminal D-West concourse, with manufacturer-rated coverage of roughly 7,500 to 19,400 square feet per hour depending on the model. Employees map and assign the routes; the robots use laser-based navigation, cameras and sensors to detect passengers, luggage and obstacles and adjust their paths, while custodians oversee routing, performance and maintenance. The airport says the robots are not replacing custodians but handling repetitive floor care so staff can focus on restrooms and high-touch surfaces. More robots are budgeted for Terminals A, D and E and the airport subway tunnel.

whyItMatters: Floor care is steady, repetitive labor that eats hours every night in terminals, FBO lobbies and hangar offices. Moving it to a robot frees people for the tasks customers notice, such as clean restrooms and a tidy ramp lounge, without adding staff. Ask for the robot's real coverage on your own floors, since rated figures assume open space, and count the overnight labor hours it would replace.
